open_points.subject: State 1 and State 2 authority
open_points.text: State 1 says "Draft of 2026-10-31" and "The state is not yet closed by question rounds", while the State 2 files contain "Accepted decision" rules derived from it and are themselves headed "Draft of 2026-10-31".
open_points.question: Which draft provisions are authoritative inputs for later states and code, and are the State 2 decision texts accepted as written or only their underlying proposals?
options: Treat every displayed Accepted decision and all State 1 model text as normative despite the draft statuses
Require State 1 and each State 2 document to be explicitly closed before continuing
Treat only the separately identified owner answers as accepted and re-derive the final wording
open_points.default_guess: Treat the displayed Accepted decisions and the State 1 model text they cite as normative.

open_points.subject: Agent-session registration check
open_points.text: A10 says "A call with agent authority is accepted only when ... the session it names is registered", but A11 says "Cabinet Kernel registers a session when its agent session starts" and permits registering a new or ended identity.
open_points.question: How can the registration operation pass A10 when the session being registered does not yet exist?
options: Exempt registration from the registered-session check and check only the Kernel token
Use a separate non-agent-authority Kernel operation for registration
Require some prior provisional session registration outside this operation
open_points.default_guess: Exempt registration from the registered-session check while still requiring the Kernel token.

open_points.subject: Authorization of pointer withdrawal
open_points.text: A10 checks "for an operation on a project — the project is in that session's set", while withdrawal is expressed as an operation on a pointer and A08 only says it occurs "on a project of its session's set".
open_points.question: When Kernel withdraws a pointer, must the request also name a project, or must Registry resolve the pointer's project before applying the session-set check, and what is returned when either the pointer or its project is outside the set?
options: Require both pointer id and project id and verify they match
Resolve the pointer first and authorize against its stored project
Treat the session's active project as the project when none is supplied
open_points.default_guess: Resolve the pointer's stored project internally and return the same not-found result for an absent pointer or a pointer outside the session set.

open_points.subject: Order of agent-authority checks
open_points.text: A09 refuses an operation outside a token's row, while A10 separately checks the Kernel token, registration, project membership, project existence and archived status; no order is stated when several checks fail together.
open_points.question: Which refusal takes precedence when a call simultaneously has an unauthorized operation, an unregistered session, a missing or out-of-set project, or an archived project?
options: Authenticate and authorize the operation, then session, membership/existence, and record state
Perform all checks but collapse every agent-authority failure to not found
Specify a different fixed precedence per operation
open_points.default_guess: Check token and operation first, then session, then membership using a non-disclosing not-found result, then project state.

open_points.subject: Kernel's right to end a session
open_points.text: A11 says "Cabinet Kernel ends a session when its agent session ends", but A09's Cabinet Kernel operations do not include ending an agent session.
open_points.question: Is ending a session an operation allowed to the Cabinet Kernel token?
options: Add end-session to Cabinet Kernel's A09 row
Make session ending an owner-only operation
Use an internal Kernel channel distinct from the service-token operations
open_points.default_guess: Add end-session to Cabinet Kernel's allowed operations.

open_points.subject: Ending and the access version
open_points.text: A12 says owner actions including "ending the session" state the access version and its formal invariant says "accepted change of x => version(x)' = version(x) + 1", while A11 says ending "removes the session's record" and "no record of x remains".
open_points.question: Does an accepted end increment a version that is then discarded, return a final version, or merely check the stated version without moving it?
options: Check the version, delete the record, and perform no observable increment
Increment and return a final tombstone version before deletion
Keep an ended session record carrying the incremented version
open_points.default_guess: Check the supplied version and atomically delete the session without an observable increment.

open_points.subject: One session action changing several access facts
open_points.text: The access version "moves by one with each accepted change of its granted set, its active project or its pending request"; granting may also make a project active, revoking the active project clears it, and accepting a request may add a grant, change the active project and clear the request.
open_points.question: Does one accepted action increment the access version once, or once for every access fact it changes?
options: Increment once per accepted action regardless of how many access facts change
Increment once for each changed access fact
Split compound actions into separately versioned changes
open_points.default_guess: Increment once per accepted atomic action.

open_points.subject: Granting an already granted project while activating it
open_points.text: A12 requires that changing the active project moves the version, while A05 says "granting a project already granted leaves the access version" even though the grant action may also make that project active.
open_points.question: What happens when the owner grants an already granted project and asks to make it active while another project or none is active?
options: Treat it as an active-project change and increment once
Treat the entire grant as a no-op and leave the active project unchanged
Refuse combining activation with a repeated grant
open_points.default_guess: Change the active project and increment the access version once.

open_points.subject: Owner-session activity
open_points.text: The session ends after "30 minutes without an owner action", but the text does not define whether reads, refused changes, confirmation-page views, or other authenticated requests are owner actions.
open_points.question: Exactly which requests refresh the owner session's inactivity deadline?
options: Every authenticated owner-interface request
Only accepted owner actions, including reads
Only accepted state-changing actions
open_points.default_guess: Refresh it on every successfully authenticated owner-interface request, including reads, but not on refused requests.

open_points.subject: Sign-in lockout window
open_points.text: "After 5 refused sign-ins within 15 minutes, every sign-in ... is refused for the next 15 minutes" does not say when that second interval starts, whether attempts during lockout extend it or count toward another lockout, whether success clears earlier failures, or whether restart clears the counter.
open_points.question: What is the exact state machine for failure counting and lockout, including concurrent attempts and restart?
options: Lock for 15 minutes from the fifth failure; ignore attempts during lockout; clear failures on success; reset on restart
Use a sliding window in which every locked-out attempt is another failure and may extend lockout
Persist failures and lockout across restarts
open_points.default_guess: Lock atomically for 15 minutes from the fifth failure, do not extend it with locked-out attempts, clear the failure window on success, and reset it on restart.

open_points.subject: Confirmation challenge and confirmation id
open_points.text: A13 says "A confirmation step ... is valid only in the session that showed it, and once", while State 1 says Registry "keeps no Confirmation record" and A14 says a confirmation id is minted only after an accepted confirmed change.
open_points.question: What value proves the pre-action confirmation, what exact action, target, revision and inputs is it bound to, where is its one-use state kept, and is that value distinct from the confirmation id written after acceptance?
options: Keep a one-use confirmation challenge in temporary owner-session state and mint the audit confirmation id only on acceptance
Use one signed self-contained value as both challenge and final confirmation id, with a replay store
Rely only on the ordinary CSRF value and the submitted action fields
open_points.default_guess: Use a separate one-use challenge stored in the owner session, bound to the complete action and current revision; mint the audit confirmation id only when the change commits.

open_points.subject: Publication and supersession instants
open_points.text: A07 stores the new pointer and marks the prior pointer superseded "with its instant" in one transaction, but does not say whether the new pointer's published instant and the old pointer's superseded instant must be the same instant or how they are ordered.
open_points.question: What timestamps are recorded for the two changes made by one publish transaction?
options: Use one transaction instant for both facts
Read the clock separately and require superseded_at no later than published_at
Allow unrelated instants taken anywhere during the transaction
open_points.default_guess: Use one transaction instant for both the supersession and publication.

open_points.subject: Concurrent publish and withdrawal
open_points.text: Publishes of one type are serialised, but no ordering rule covers a publish racing a withdrawal of the current pointer or two withdrawals racing each other.
open_points.question: How are these operations linearized, and which operations are accepted or refused for each possible race?
options: Serialize every publish and withdrawal for one project and type
Serialize only operations on the same pointer
Give publication fixed precedence over withdrawal
open_points.default_guess: Serialize all publish and withdrawal operations for the same project and type; outcomes follow the resulting order.

open_points.subject: Service-token publication rule
open_points.text: A08 says both "A pointer is published and withdrawn by Cabinet Kernel" and "No service token has the right to publish or withdraw", while A09 identifies Cabinet Kernel as a service with a service token and grants those operations.
open_points.question: Does "No service token" exclude Cabinet Kernel's agent-authority token, or is A08 rule 2 intended to refer only to document-owner and other non-Kernel services?
options: Rewrite the rule to exclude only non-Kernel service tokens
Treat Kernel's agent-authority credential as something other than a service token
Remove publish and withdraw from Kernel
open_points.default_guess: Interpret the prohibition as applying to every non-Kernel service token only.

open_points.subject: Re-adding a removed artifact type
open_points.text: A22 defines adding and removing types but does not say what happens if a later release declares the same removed type again while its old pointers remain.
open_points.question: May the same type be re-added, and if so do new versions continue after the old maximum, does its former published pointer become the current pointer again, and may old pointers be withdrawn?
options: Permit re-addition and continue the old version history
Forbid re-adding a removed type name
Treat the re-added name as a fresh version namespace while keeping old history separate
open_points.default_guess: Permit re-addition only with the same owner service, continue after the old maximum version, and treat any still-published old pointer as the current one.

open_points.subject: Replay after artifact-type removal
open_points.text: A01 says a publish repeat "answers the pointer it made, whatever its status now" and only explicitly puts access and archive checks first; A22 says after type removal "publishing that type ... [is] refused as an unknown type".
open_points.question: Does a retry of an already accepted publish still return its pointer after that type has been removed from the release?
options: Refuse it as an unknown type before replay lookup
Return the old pointer because the retry makes no publication
Return it only to the owner, but refuse Kernel retries
open_points.default_guess: Apply the current vocabulary check first and refuse the retry as an unknown type.

open_points.subject: Concurrent audited changes
open_points.text: A14 requires each accepted listed change and its audit entry to commit together, while M09 requires globally increasing unique sequence numbers, but no rule says how concurrent unrelated changes obtain and order those numbers.
open_points.question: Must concurrent independently valid changes both succeed with consecutive audit sequence numbers, and what defines their order?
options: Serialize audit-number allocation and let both changes succeed in commit order
Allow one action to be refused and retried on a sequence collision
Allocate numbers outside transactions and permit gaps after rollback
open_points.default_guess: Serialize transactional sequence allocation and order entries by the commits of their changes, with no gaps caused by failed transactions.

open_points.subject: Audit sequence high-water mark
open_points.text: A15 says "Sequence numbers are never reused" and the next entry continues from "the last number ever written", even though the only operation may erase every entry and State 1 defines no durable audit-sequence counter.
open_points.question: Where is the last-ever sequence retained after all entries containing it have been erased and the instance restarts?
options: Add a durable audit high-water value outside the entries
Never erase the most recent entry
Derive the next number from surviving entries and permit reuse after complete erasure
open_points.default_guess: Persist a separate audit sequence high-water value that erasure never removes.

open_points.subject: Meaning of today for audit erasure
open_points.text: A15 refuses "a date not later than today" and removes entries before "the start of that date (UTC)", but it does not explicitly say whether "today" is the UTC date or the owner's Europe/Madrid date.
open_points.question: Which calendar and time zone determine whether the supplied date is later than today?
options: UTC date, matching the erasure boundary
Owner's configured local date, with removal still using UTC midnight
Owner's browser date
open_points.default_guess: Use the current UTC date.

open_points.subject: Customer mapping inputs during import
open_points.text: A16's mapping lists "each Customer the import will make and the projects it will link", while M04 requires the owner to give every such Customer its kind and name and to say whether the old v1 value is its tax id.
open_points.question: Must the preview collect and show each new Customer's name, kind and tax-id decision, and must confirmation bind all of those values?
options: Collect, display and bind all Customer mapping values in the preview
Import provisional Customers and complete them afterward
Derive the values from the export without owner input
open_points.default_guess: Collect and show all required Customer values and bind them into the confirmed mapping.

open_points.subject: Completeness of the import preview
open_points.text: The preview shows each project "with its id, status, rooms and pointers" but does not require it to show the embedded object, source timestamps, customer link, revisions assigned on import, pointer statuses and versions, or other transformations that the transaction stores.
open_points.question: Which complete set of imported and transformed facts must the owner see before confirming the mapping?
options: Show every stored fact or an explicit before-to-after mapping for it
Show only the fields listed in A16 rule 1
Show a summary and make the full normalized import downloadable separately
open_points.default_guess: Show every resulting record and every transformed or discarded source value before confirmation.

open_points.subject: Definition of a malformed import record
open_points.text: A16 says "a malformed record" refuses the whole import, while A22 names only an undeclared artifact type as one example and States 5 and 6 are assigned only the file format.
open_points.question: Which semantic failures make a record malformed, including broken links, duplicate ids inside the file, invalid statuses, nonconsecutive pointer versions, multiple published pointers, missing required values, invalid timestamps and owner-service mismatches?
options: Declare and validate all model and cross-record invariants at preview and confirmation
Treat only syntactic/schema failures and undeclared types as malformed
Normalize or repair inconsistent source records during mapping
open_points.default_guess: Refuse any file that violates a State 1 model invariant, reference integrity, vocabulary rule or pointer-history invariant.

open_points.subject: Conflicts in projects not selected for import
open_points.text: The preview names "every id that conflicts with one production holds", rule 3 says "Any conflict ... refuses the whole import", but the accepted transaction stores only "every picked project".
open_points.question: Does a conflicting id belonging only to an unpicked project, room or pointer refuse the import?
options: Check conflicts only in the selected import closure
Reject conflicts anywhere in the uploaded file
Require the export file itself to contain only selected projects
open_points.default_guess: Check and refuse only conflicts in the selected projects and their reachable records.

open_points.subject: Imported customer_ref provenance
open_points.text: A16 allows a conflict involving "a Registry-minted customer_ref" from the file, while M04 states that no v1 customer_ref was minted by Registry and that the import makes a new Customer for every distinct v1 value.
open_points.question: Can this one VPS import ever preserve a source customer_ref, and if so how does Registry prove that it was Registry-minted rather than merely UUID-shaped?
options: Never preserve a VPS v1 customer_ref; always mint new Customer identities
Trust an explicit provenance marker in the migration file
Infer provenance from the identifier's UUID format
open_points.default_guess: Never preserve a customer_ref from this v1 source; mint and map every Customer identity anew.

open_points.subject: Concurrent import confirmation
open_points.text: A16 checks conflicts "at confirmation" and then writes the import transaction, but does not say that the conflict check, closure-absence check and writes share one serialization boundary with ordinary creates or another confirmation.
open_points.question: What happens when two confirmations run concurrently, or when a normal create introduces a conflicting id between the recheck and the import writes?
options: Perform all checks and writes in one serializable transaction
Use unique constraints and translate any collision into the specified whole-import refusal
Lock the whole Registry against writes during confirmation
open_points.default_guess: Run the closure check, conflict recheck and all writes in one serializable transaction and refuse the losing import without partial state.

open_points.subject: Verification that secrets are random
open_points.text: A17 requires every secret to be "at least 32 bytes generated at random by the owner's vault", but Registry can check length and equality, not how a supplied value was generated.
open_points.question: Is random generation an external owner obligation or a startup condition Registry must somehow verify?
options: Make generation provenance an external operational requirement and check only measurable properties
Require a vault-generated metadata or signed envelope proving provenance
Replace the requirement with a measurable entropy/encoding rule
open_points.default_guess: Treat vault generation as an external obligation and have Registry check only encoding, byte length and inequality.

open_points.subject: Secret byte encoding
open_points.text: A17 requires a secret to be "at least 32 bytes", but configuration values have no declared encoding or rule for whether length is measured before or after decoding.
open_points.question: What representation is accepted for secrets and exactly which bytes are counted and compared?
options: Require a specified encoded random-byte format such as base64 and count decoded bytes
Accept UTF-8 text and count its encoded bytes
Count configuration characters rather than bytes
open_points.default_guess: Require one canonical encoded form and require at least 32 decoded random bytes.

open_points.subject: Configuration validation surface
open_points.text: A17 says "A missing, malformed or unknown item fails the start" and that the configuration "names the store", but does not enumerate valid configuration items or define a malformed store, credential, token name or extra item.
open_points.question: What is the closed configuration schema and which store connectivity, permissions, schema-version and encryption checks must pass before Registry serves?
options: Define a closed schema and verify store access plus schema compatibility at startup
Validate only presence and basic string forms, leaving store failures to first use
Allow unknown configuration entries and reject only unknown Registry-specific keys
open_points.default_guess: Use a closed configuration schema and verify store connectivity, required permissions and schema compatibility before serving.

open_points.subject: Backup schedule and failure handling
open_points.text: A18 says "Once a day the store is backed up" but does not define the scheduling boundary, maximum interval, behavior after downtime or failure, retries, alerting, or whether Registry may continue serving without a recent successful backup.
open_points.question: What exact condition satisfies the daily-backup rule, and what must happen when a backup is missed or fails?
options: Require at least one successful backup in every rolling 24-hour period and alert/block release on failure
Run once per local calendar day and retry the next day only
Attempt daily but impose no availability or alerting consequence on failure
open_points.default_guess: Require a successful backup at least every 24 hours, retry and alert on failure, while allowing Registry to continue serving.

open_points.subject: Thirty-day backup deletion boundary
open_points.text: Backups are "kept 30 days; older backups are deleted" and an erasure must disappear from backups "at most 30 days after it", but no deletion cadence or inclusive boundary is stated.
open_points.question: Is the limit exactly 30 times 24 hours, 30 calendar days, or a daily cleanup that can retain a backup beyond 30 days, and when is deletion required to run?
options: Delete each backup no later than exactly 30 times 24 hours after creation
Delete at the first daily cleanup after 30 calendar days
Keep the most recent 30 daily backups regardless of elapsed age
open_points.default_guess: Delete each backup no later than 30 times 24 hours after its creation.

open_points.subject: Restore-test instance classification
open_points.text: A18 restores a production backup "into a temporary instance on VM Platform" while State 0 says every instance other than production is a test instance that "holds ... no production personal data"; A18 then says "a test instance never receives a production backup".
open_points.question: What kind of instance is the temporary restore target, and under which production-data guarantees may it hold the restored personal data?
options: Define a separate isolated production-restore instance on VM Platform
Treat it as a test instance and create an explicit exception to the no-production-data rule
Test only an anonymised or synthetic backup instead of the production backup
open_points.default_guess: Define it as a separate isolated production-restore environment, not a test instance, with production-equivalent access controls and mandatory destruction.

open_points.subject: Restore-test acceptance and release gate
open_points.text: Before release the owner "checks that it starts (A17) and answers", without saying which integrity checks or answers are required or whether a failed or absent restore test blocks the release.
open_points.question: What exact restore test must pass, how is its result recorded, and is release forbidden when it fails?
options: Run a declared integrity and representative-read suite, record the result, and block release on failure
Require only successful startup and one health response
Make the exercise advisory and allow release after a recorded failure
open_points.default_guess: Require a recorded integrity check plus representative authenticated reads and block the release unless it passes.

open_points.subject: Reapplying erasures after production restore
open_points.text: After restore the owner repeats "every erasure made after the backup's instant, as the owner's retention review recorded it", but no durable source or complete format for that external record is defined, and Registry's own later audit entries are lost in the restored backup or may already have been erased.
open_points.question: What authoritative record enumerates all customer, project and audit-log erasures after the backup, and how is completeness verified before serving resumes?
options: Maintain an external append-only erasure ledger with identities, action type and time
Use audit exports retained outside the backed-up store
Rely on the owner's manual notes without an automated completeness check
open_points.default_guess: Maintain an external append-only erasure ledger and require its post-backup entries to be replayed and verified before serving.

open_points.subject: Encryption guarantee
open_points.text: A18 requires encrypted backups, an owner-held key and encrypted disks, but does not define the encryption format, authenticated-integrity requirement, key identity or rotation, or which component verifies those properties.
open_points.question: What measurable encryption and key-management conditions must backups and disks satisfy?
options: Declare an authenticated backup-encryption format and a verified platform disk-encryption profile
Leave algorithms and verification entirely to deployment
Accept any mechanism described by the owner as encrypted
open_points.default_guess: Require authenticated encryption for backup files and a documented, checked VM Platform disk-encryption profile, with keys outside the backups.

open_points.subject: Release dependency boundary and digest
open_points.text: A20 says a release names "every dependency it runs with, at an exact version, with its digest" but does not define whether this includes transitive packages, language runtime, operating-system libraries, database engine and other executables, or what artifact the digest covers.
open_points.question: What is the closed dependency boundary, and which exact artifact is hashed and verified for each dependency?
options: Include all application and transitive runtime artifacts in the release or container and hash those artifacts
Cover only direct Python packages
Treat the complete container or machine image as the single dependency artifact
open_points.default_guess: Pin and hash every direct and transitive application dependency plus the runtime in a reproducible release image; manage host components under a separately fixed platform image.

open_points.subject: Replay comparison after a record changes
open_points.text: A01 compares a repeat with "the same supplied facts" and returns the record "as it stands now", but State 1 records only the request id and current editable facts, which corrections may replace; it defines no stored original create facts.
open_points.question: Against what durable value is a replay compared after the project or Customer has been corrected, and where is that original value stored?
options: Store a canonical snapshot or digest of the original supplied create facts with the record
Compare against the record's current facts
After any correction, refuse all uses of the old request id
open_points.default_guess: Persist a canonical original-create comparison snapshot or digest beside the request id until erasure or anonymisation removes it.

open_points.subject: Concurrent creates with one request id
open_points.text: A01 defines behavior when "an existing record" already carries the request id and declares uniqueness, but it does not state the result of two simultaneous creates that both observe no existing record.
open_points.question: Must equal concurrent calls both succeed with the same record, and must different concurrent calls produce one success and one specified conflict rather than an internal error?
options: Serialize by model and request id; equal calls return one record and unequal calls give one success and one refusal
Allow one call to fail with a generic concurrency error and be retried
Refuse both calls when the request id is contested concurrently
open_points.default_guess: Serialize by model and request id; equal calls return the same record, while for unequal facts the first commits and the other is refused.

open_points.subject: Replay checks after other state changes
open_points.text: Only publish retries explicitly say "The checks of the call come first"; the general replay rule does not say whether a room retry after project archive, or a project-create retry after its customer became erased, restricted or ended, returns the original record or is refused by current preconditions.
open_points.question: For project, Customer and room creates, which current authorization and parent/customer-state checks run before replay recognition?
options: Authenticate and authorize first, then return any matching replay without rechecking mutable business preconditions
Run every current precondition before replay lookup
Define separate precedence for each create operation
open_points.default_guess: Authenticate and authorize first, then recognize an equal replay before mutable project or customer-state preconditions.

open_points.subject: Blank and whitespace definition
open_points.text: A02 defines blank with "strip(v) = \"\"" but does not define the Unicode whitespace set, Unicode version or whether the operation applies only to string-valued facts.
open_points.question: Exactly which code points count as whitespace, and how are non-string required and optional values handled by this rule?
options: Use the implementation language's Unicode whitespace semantics at the release's fixed runtime version, for strings only
Declare an explicit immutable whitespace code-point set
Treat only ASCII spaces, tabs and line breaks as whitespace
open_points.default_guess: Apply the fixed runtime's Unicode whitespace definition to string values only and validate non-string values by their own schemas.

open_points.subject: Repeated grant of an archived project
open_points.text: A05 accepts "granting a project already in a session's set" as unchanged, while State 0 says granting an archived project is refused and archiving leaves an existing grant in the set.
open_points.question: If an archived project is already granted and the owner grants it again, is the call an accepted no-op or refused because archived-project validation comes first?
options: Refuse because archived-project validation precedes repeated-transition detection
Accept it unchanged because it adds no archived grant
Accept only when the action does not also request activation
open_points.default_guess: Refuse it because the archived-project precondition runs before no-op detection.

open_points.subject: Making an already-active archived project active
open_points.text: A05 accepts "making the active project active again", while R0-70 says "Making an archived project active is refused" and also says a project archived while active stays active.
open_points.question: What happens when the owner selects as active the same project that remained active after being archived?
options: Refuse because archived-project validation comes first
Accept unchanged because no activation occurs
Automatically clear the archived active project
open_points.default_guess: Refuse the explicit action while leaving the existing active value unchanged.

open_points.subject: Validation of inputs to repeated transitions
open_points.text: A05 accepts ending an already ended relationship and keeps the old date, while R0-84 refuses an end date later than today; similar no-op transitions may carry stale versions or otherwise invalid inputs.
open_points.question: Are input validation and stale-version checks performed before deciding that a transition is already in its target state?
options: Validate authentication, version and all supplied values first, then detect a no-op
Detect the current target state first and ignore all unused invalid input
Specify exceptions per transition
open_points.default_guess: Perform authentication, stale-version and input validation before no-op detection.

open_points.subject: Orders of embedded collections
open_points.text: A06 orders the named list operations, but project cards, agent projections, session-access answers and import mappings also contain collections of rooms, pointers, granted project ids, projects or Customers whose order is not declared.
open_points.question: Do the corresponding list-operation orders apply to every embedded collection, and what orders apply to granted ids and import-preview collections?
options: Declare an order for every collection-valued answer in State 2
Treat model sets as unordered and let State 6 choose serialization order
Reuse list-room and list-artifact orders where applicable and sort identities lexically elsewhere
open_points.default_guess: Reuse the room and artifact list orders for embedded projections and sort otherwise unordered identity sets lexically; explicitly order every import-preview collection.

open_points.subject: Artifact-type comparison in list order
open_points.text: A06 orders artifacts "by type" but rule 7 defines comparisons only for "Names" and "identities"; it does not say how artifact vocabulary values compare.
open_points.question: What total order is used for artifact types?
options: Unicode code-point order of the stored type value
The order in which types appear in the release vocabulary
A separately declared ordinal for each type
open_points.default_guess: Use Unicode code-point order of the type value.
